body.statement: For every \(\theta\in\Theta\) and integer \(k\ge2\), \(m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A\), and therefore \(Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k\).
body.justification: Multilinearity and independent-source cancellation isolate the observable flag equation.
body.gap: Kivva et al. derive scalar higher-moment ratios for one changing component; the vector projection that removes a jointly varying latent profile is new.
body.consumer: The lemma supplies the estimable moment restriction used by the identification functional and every subsequent inference procedure.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta\) and \(k\geq 2\).  Put
\[
 v_k=\alpha^k u_k,
 \qquad
 w_k=\bigl(\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e})-\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,0})\bigr)_{e=1}^{E-1}.
\]
The source moment generating functions are finite in a neighborhood of zero, so the relevant cumulants exist.  By source independence, the joint moment generating function of \(\alpha U_e\) and \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) factorizes.  Taking the degree-\(k\) derivative of its logarithm gives additivity of cumulants of independent sums, and hence, by the definition of \(c_k\),
\[
 c_k=v_k+w_k=\alpha^k u_k+w_k. \tag{1}
\]
Multilinearity of the joint cumulant and the structural equation for \(Y_e\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \kappa_k(Y_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 &=\beta\kappa_k(T_e)
   +\gamma\kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
   +\kappa_k(\epsilon_y,T_e,\ldots,T_e).
 \end{aligned}                                       \tag{2}
\]
The last term in (2) is zero because \(\epsilon_y\) is independent of \(T_e\) and \(k\geq2\).  On expanding each of the remaining \(k-1\) arguments \(T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e}\), every term containing both \(U_e\) and \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) is a mixed cumulant of independent groups and is zero.  Thus
\[
 \kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)=\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(U_e)
 =\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(\epsilon_{u,e}).              \tag{3}
\]
Subtracting the environment-zero version of (2), and using (3) and the definitions of \(m_k,c_k,u_k\), yields
\[
 m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k.              \tag{4}
\]
The latent-profile-plane assumption gives \(u_k\in A\), so (4) lies in \(A\).  The calibration-rank assumption makes the displayed formula for \(Q_A\) well defined, and that formula is the orthogonal projector with kernel \(A\).  Applying it to (4) proves
\[
 Q_A m_k=\beta Q_Ac_k,
\]
as asserted.
